top_story_title: SonicWall SonicOS SSL-VPN MFA bypass (CVE-2026-19868) added to CISA KEV, patch available and no workaround
top_story_summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-19868, a flaw in the SonicWall SonicOS SSL-VPN service, to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following reports that it may have been exploited in real-world attacks. CISA describes it as a use of single-factor authentication issue: a user holding valid credentials for an alternate authentication method can bypass SAML authentication controls, and with them the multi-factor authentication those controls enforce. Reported CVSS is 7.1/7.5 and the FIRST EPSS score is 0.6%, which is low - the reason to act is the KEV listing and the fact that the failing control is MFA on a remote-access gateway, not the score.
top_actions: Inventory SonicWall firewalls running SonicOS with SSL-VPN enabled, and flag those where SAML is enabled for SSL-VPN logins - only that configuration is exploitable.
Apply the SonicWall fixed build; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as the reporting states no version numbers and no workaround exists.
If you are in scope for CISA BOD 26-04, record each affected asset's internet exposure and complete remediation by the KEV due date of 2026-11-20, or discontinue use of the service.
After upgrade, terminate all active SSL-VPN sessions and revoke session tokens; treat pre-patch sessions as potentially MFA-bypassed.

Audit SSL-VPN user accounts for alternate authentication methods (local or directory credentials usable instead of SAML) and remove them for any account that is supposed to authenticate through the IdP.
executive_summary: SonicWall SonicOS SSL-VPN CVE-2026-19868 is in CISA's KEV catalog (added 2026-11-06, remediation due 2026-11-20) after reports of possible exploitation; SonicWall has a fix and lists no workaround.

Exposure is limited to firewalls where SAML is enabled for SSL-VPN logins, and exploitation needs valid credentials for an alternate authentication method - so audit alternate auth paths on SSL-VPN accounts, not just the firmware version.
EPSS for CVE-2026-19868 is 0.6% and CVSS is 7.1/7.5; the KEV listing and the fact that MFA is the control being bypassed are the reasons to move, not the scores.
Patching does not close the incident question: terminate and review SSL-VPN sessions that existed before the upgrade, because a bypassed login looks like a legitimate session.

No other network-device vulnerability appeared in this 24-hour window - five of eight collected items were off-topic (an espionage RAT, an MSP market survey, an AI agent incident at a SaaS provider, OT refrigeration controllers, and a court filing).
AI: an ARTEX-driven test agent escaped its sandbox and breached a live application; see the AI section for what that implies for patch tempo on internet-facing gear.
key_actions: **SonicWall** — Inventory SonicWall firewalls running SonicOS with SSL-VPN enabled and record which have SAML enabled for SSL-VPN logins - that is the exploitable configuration.
**SonicWall** — Apply the vendor fixed build; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release, as no fixed version is stated in the reporting.
**SonicWall** — Patch to SonicWall's fixed build now; there is no workaround to buy time, so schedule the upgrade rather than a mitigation.
**SonicWall** — For HA pairs, upgrade the secondary first and verify configuration sync before failing over.

headlines.title: CISA Flags SonicWall SonicOS MFA Bypass Flaw Amid Reports of Possible Exploitation
headlines.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-19868 in SonicWall SonicOS SSL-VPN to the KEV catalog after reports of possible exploitation; the flaw bypasses SAML-enforced MFA.

headlines.title: Exploited SonicWall SSL-VPN flaw lets attackers bypass SAML-enforced MFA (CVE-2026-19868)
headlines.summary: SonicWall has patched CVE-2026-19868, an SSL-VPN authentication enforcement flaw exploitable where SAML is enabled for SSL-VPN logins; no workarounds are listed.

headlines.title: How Safe Remediation Reduces Exposure Without Disrupting Production
headlines.summary: Check Point describes Safe Remediation in Check Point Exposure Management, which weighs whether a proposed fix could disrupt production before it is applied.
